Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The players are out in the middle. Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Sediqullah Atal to open for Afghanistan. Richard Ngarava to bowl first.
...THE CHASE...

Afghanistan will be pleased with their efforts. They weren't at their very best in the Powerplay but after that, they did really well. Rashid, Mujeeb and Omarzai were excellent but they'll be slightly disappointed that they let the last pair form a small stand which helped the hosts get over 120. They'll still back themselves to chase it down but it could be a tricky chase. Join us shortly for it.

From 78 for 3, they slipped to 106 for 9. The last pair though batted really well. They converted ones into twos and managed to get over the 120-run mark which looked difficult when that collapse happened. We still feel it's slightly under par but they do have something to bowl at.

Zimbabwe have crawled their way to close to 130 and it’s all thanks to the last pair. At one stage though, it seemed like they would get a lot more. The top order got them off to a decent start but yet again the middle order failed to make most of it.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz(WK), Sediqullah Atal, Zubaid Akbari, Darwish Rasooli, Azmatullah Omarzai, Mohammad Nabi, Gulbadin Naib, Rashid Khan(C), Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Naveen-ul-Haq, Fazalhaq Farooqi.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Tadiwanashe Marumani(WK), Brian Bennett, Dion Myers, Wessly Madhevere, Sikandar Raza(C), Tashinga Musekiwa, Wellington Masakadza, Faraz Akram, Richard Ngarava, Blessing Muzarabani, Trevor Gwandu.
TOSS - Afghanistan have won the toss and ELECTED TO BOWL!

Zimbabwe's problem has been their middle order! They really need the likes of Raza, Burl and Wessly Madhevere to get some runs. The top order has performed decently but it is the middle order which needs to step up and if that happens, they'll surely be in with a good chance. Can they upset the odds here?

The introduction of Darwish Rasooli came in handy as he played a fine knock for his side to take them to a decent score in the last game. The question is, will we see the visitors play an extra spinner this time around? Will we see Noor Ahmad get a chance in place of a seamer? Usually teams don't change their winning combination but we will have to wait to find out.

It is time for the decider! The series is level at 1-1 with the hosts taking the first one and visitors bouncing back strongly in the second. Afghanistan are surely favourites to win the series but we have seen Zimbabwe causing upsets in the past. It has been quite a good contest between bat and ball so far in the first two games and we expect nothing less here.
